title: PATCH /api/profile does not apply the registration rules to username and email (empty, markup, any length, invalid email)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH PATCH /api/profile › username change follows the registration rules (charset, length); › username cannot be changed to an empty string; › email change rejects invalid addresses
cause: shared/schema.ts:555 updateProfileSchema is createInsertSchema(users).pick(...) so username/email are plain z.string() without the trim/min/max/regex/email checks of insertUserSchema (shared/schema.ts:526-527); server/auth.ts:474/481 also skip the duplicate check for an empty string because of `if (result.data.username)`
fix: Reuse the field schemas: export usernameSchema/emailSchema from insertUserSchema and use them in updateProfileSchema (.extend({ username: usernameSchema, email: emailSchema })); compare with `!== undefined` instead of truthiness before the duplicate checks

title: Usernames and emails are unique only case-sensitively (impersonation, duplicate accounts per mailbox)
evidence: register Casexyz → 201, register casexyz → 201; email a@x.test exists, register A@X.TEST → 201; PATCH /api/profile {username: existing.toLowerCase()} → 200, {email: existing.toUpperCase()} → 200
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH register: validation › usernames that differ only in case are treated as duplicates; › duplicate email is rejected, also with different case; › AUTH PATCH /api/profile › username change to a case variant of an existing name is rejected; › email change: valid works, invalid format and duplicates (any case) are rejected
cause: server/storage/user-storage.ts:47 and :66 use eq(users.username, …)/eq(users.email, …) (case-sensitive) and the DB unique constraints in shared/schema.ts are on the raw text columns
fix: Normalise email to lower case on write; compare usernames with lower(): unique index on lower(username) and lower(email), and getUserByUsername/getUserByEmail using sql`lower(${users.username}) = lower(${value})` (keep display case for usernames)

title: CORS reflects any Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
evidence: GET /api/user, Origin: https://evil.example → ACAO: https://evil.example, ACAC: true; OPTIONS /api/profile preflight from evil.example with x-csrf-token → approved
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH sessions and cookies › CORS does not grant credentialed access to arbitrary origins; › CORS preflight from a foreign origin does not allow the CSRF header
cause: server/index.ts:43-46 cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }) for every environment. SameSite=Lax currently keeps the cookie off cross-site fetches, but any same-site origin (other subdomain, http variant) can read /api/csrf-token and /api/user and then make authenticated writes — the CSRF protection relies entirely on SameSite
fix: Use an allow-list: cors({ origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGINS?.split(',') ?? false, credentials: true }); the SPA is same-origin and does not need CORS at all

title: Login, register and logout are not CSRF protected (login CSRF via plain HTML form, forced logout)
evidence: POST /api/login without x-csrf-token → 200; urlencoded form body from Origin evil.example → 200 + session cookie; POST /api/register without token → 201; POST /api/logout without token → 200
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH login › login requires a CSRF token (no login CSRF); › an urlencoded cross-site form cannot log a browser into an account; › AUTH register: validation › register requires a CSRF token like every other state-changing request; › AUTH sessions and cookies › logout requires a CSRF token (no forced logout from other sites)
cause: server/auth.ts:248/384/432 are registered inside setupAuth (server/routes/index.ts:146) before the global app.use("/api", validateCsrf) at server/routes/index.ts:225 and do not add validateCsrf themselves (unlike /api/profile); server/index.ts:49 also accepts urlencoded bodies, so a cross-site <form> works without preflight
fix: Add validateCsrf to the three routes (the client already fetches /api/csrf-token before login/register), or move the global CSRF middleware before setupAuth's routes; drop express.urlencoded if no form posts are needed

title: Frozen (and IP/device-banned) accounts can still change profile and password
evidence: admin sets isFrozen=1; POST /api/comments → 403 ACCOUNT_FROZEN, but PATCH /api/profile {bio} → 200 and PATCH /api/profile/password → 200
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH frozen accounts › a frozen account cannot change its profile; › a frozen account cannot change its password
cause: Both routes are registered in setupAuth (server/auth.ts:468, :504), which runs before app.use(banCheckMiddleware) at server/routes/index.ts:149, so the freeze/ban checks in server/middleware/ban-check.ts never run for them (same for POST /api/login)
fix: Register banCheckMiddleware before the auth routes (it only needs req.user, i.e. right after passport.session() in setupAuth), or move the profile routes into a router mounted after it

title: Public profile and user search leak moderation state and other users' email addresses
evidence: anonymous GET /api/users/<frozen user> → isShadowBanned:1, isFrozen:1, freezeReason:"internal-note-…", adminGroupId, emailVerified; GET /api/users/search?q=<other> → email "srchme…@e2e.test"; a shadow-banned user sees isShadowBanned:1 in GET /api/user
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH public profile and privacy › public profile of another user exposes no moderation or internal fields; › user search does not return other users' email addresses; › AUTH GET /api/user › a shadow-banned user cannot see the shadow ban in /api/user
cause: server/routes/users.ts:299 only strips password/email and spreads the full row; server/routes/users.ts:262 uses sanitizeUser (server/storage.ts:165, only removes password) for search results; server/auth.ts:463 returns the deserialized row incl. isShadowBanned
fix: Build public user DTOs from an explicit allow-list (id, username, displayName, bio, location, website, avatarUrl, coverUrl, role, verified, karma, createdAt, isPrivate); for /api/user omit isShadowBanned/freezeReason (keep frozenUntil only if the UI needs it)

title: Changing the password does not end other sessions
evidence: session B logged in, session A changes password → 200; B GET /api/user → 200 (still logged in)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH PATCH /api/profile/password › changing the password ends the user's other sessions
cause: server/auth.ts:520-524 only updates the hash; sessions in the session table (passport.user = id) stay valid and deserializeUser (server/auth.ts:213) does not compare any password/version stamp
fix: On password change delete the user's other rows from the session table (sess->'passport'->>'user' = id, except req.sessionID) or store a passwordChangedAt/sessionVersion in the session and reject older sessions in deserializeUser; regenerate the current session id

title: PATCH /api/profile never answers on an empty body or a DB error (unhandled rejection, hanging request)
evidence: PATCH /api/profile {} → no response after 5 s (log: Unhandled Rejection "No values to set"); user A renamed to "", user B renamed to "" → no response (log: Unhandled Rejection "Failed query: update users …" unique violation)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH PATCH /api/profile › an empty update answers promptly (no hanging request); › a second account renamed to the same empty username gets a prompt 4xx (no hanging request)
cause: server/auth.ts:468-502 is an async Express 4 handler without try/catch; storage.updateUserProfile (server/storage/user-storage.ts:199 .set(mappedProfile)) throws for {} and for unique violations, the rejection is swallowed by process.on('unhandledRejection') (server/index.ts:277) and the socket stays open (resource exhaustion)
fix: Wrap the handler in try/catch → sendInternalError; answer 400 when the parsed update is empty; map unique-violation (23505) to 400 "Username already taken"/"Email already registered"; same try/catch for PATCH /api/profile/password

title: Private accounts are not private: anonymous visitors get all posts of a private user
evidence: user sets isPrivate:true (UI: "Only members can see your content"); anonymous GET /api/users/<user>/posts → 200 with 1 post
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH public profile and privacy › a private account's posts are hidden from anonymous visitors
cause: server/routes/users.ts:110-150 (and /:username/comments :152, /:username/liked :204, /:username :269) never read user.isPrivate; nothing in server/ checks it (grep isPrivate)
fix: In the /:username/* list routes return 403 (or an empty list) when user.isPrivate and the viewer is not logged in (or, per the intended rule, not a follower / not the owner/admin); reduce the profile itself to public fields

title: Profile text fields have no length limit and website accepts javascript:/data: URLs
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH PATCH /api/profile › displayName with 100k characters is rejected (sane limit ≈ 100); › bio …; › location …; › website …; › website must be an http(s) URL — javascript:, data: and vbscript: are rejected
cause: shared/schema.ts:555-567 updateProfileSchema derives plain z.string().nullable() from text columns; no .max() and no URL/scheme validation for website, which the profile page renders as a link
fix: Extend updateProfileSchema: displayName z.string().trim().max(50), bio .max(500–2000), location .max(100), website z.string().trim().max(500).url().refine(u => /^https?:\/\//i.test(u)) or '' / null

title: Login timing reveals whether a username exists
evidence: median of 5: unknown user 4 ms vs existing user with wrong password 291 ms (status and message are identical)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH login › login of an unknown user takes as long as a wrong password (no timing oracle)
cause: server/auth.ts:133-148 returns immediately when the user is not found; only existing users pay the bcrypt(12) compare at server/auth.ts:151
fix: When the user is not found, run bcrypt.compare(password, DUMMY_BCRYPT_HASH) before returning the generic failure

title: Session cookie is not Secure behind the HTTPS reverse proxy unless REQUIRE_HTTPS is set (default false)
evidence: request with X-Forwarded-Proto: https (TRUST_PROXY=true) → Set-Cookie: connect.sid=…; Path=/; Expires=…; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (no Secure)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH sessions and cookies › behind an HTTPS reverse proxy the session cookie is marked Secure
cause: server/routes/index.ts:138 secure: process.env.REQUIRE_HTTPS === 'true'; docker-compose.yml:46 and .env.example:39 default REQUIRE_HTTPS to false although the documented deployment is nginx + TLS
fix: Use cookie.secure: 'auto' (express-session sets Secure when req.secure, which honours X-Forwarded-Proto with trust proxy) or default REQUIRE_HTTPS to true in production

title: isPrivate accepts any number (5, -1, 1.5) and stores it
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH public profile and privacy › isPrivate only accepts boolean-like values
cause: shared/schema.ts:541 boolOrInt = z.union([z.boolean(), z.number()]) without restricting the number to 0/1

title: Registration reveals taken usernames/emails; no per-account login limit; no self-service account deletion
evidence: register with an existing email → 400 "Email already registered"; login limiter is 20/15 min per IP only (server/auth.ts:110), the brute_force_login anomaly rule freezes the account afterwards; no DELETE /api/user or similar route exists (only DELETE /api/admin/users/:id)
test: tests/e2e/auth-account.test.ts › AUTH register: validation › registering a taken email answers 400 with a text message (documents email enumeration, info)
fix: Optional: generic registration error + verification mail for existing addresses; add a per-username limiter (keyGenerator on req.body.username); consider a self-service delete endpoint that reuses the admin deletion transaction
